s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Numerous small blisters on ears and vermillion border
Erythematous papules and crusts on cheeks, neck, and lower arms
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient had episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Laboratory tests showed detectable PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Virologic analyses negative for multiple viruses
Bacterial cultures from blister fluid were unremarkable

shortlist.label: Parvovirus B19-associated erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Detectable PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters

shortlist.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Solar urticaria
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic skin eruption following sun exposure

raw.rationale: The presence of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin biopsy specimen, along with the patient's symptoms and lack of other explanatory factors, support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the eruption occurred after sun exposure, the presence of PVB19 DNA and antibodies points more specifically to a viral etiology

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: This condition often has a more varied presentation and is not as directly linked to PVB19 infection

rejected.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by a more severe reaction to sun exposure and does not typically present with the viral markers seen in this patient

rejected.label: Solar urticaria
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic wheals of solar urticaria, and the presence of PVB19 markers suggests a different diagnosis
